title: Graph Valid Tree
summary: Decide whether the given undirected graph is a tree containing all n vertices.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–2000 vertices labeled 0 through n−1. Up to 5000 edges, with two distinct endpoints per edge. No repeated undirected edges.

statement: Decide whether the given undirected graph is a tree containing all n vertices. A tree has one connected component and no cycles.

examples.explanation: The triangle is cyclic and leaves one vertex isolated.
Vertex 0 cannot reach either endpoint of the edge.

constraints: 1–2000 vertices labeled 0 through n−1. Up to 5000 edges, with two distinct endpoints per edge. No repeated undirected edges.
hints: Conceptual: Connectivity and acyclicity both matter.
Directional: A connected graph with n−1 edges must be a tree.
Implementation: Use disjoint sets or a traversal to count components and compare the edge count with n−1.
complexityAnalysis: O(V + E) time and space with traversal, or O(V + E α(V)) time and O(V) space with Union-Find.
